text.p: Italian debt markets proved sturdy in the face of profit-taking in afternoon trade, recovering some ground from the day's lows and hauling the September LIFFE future back above 134.00, although the mood was more reflective.
"Sentiment is still positive and people are not convinced the market is going to go down dramatically," a broker in London said.

The September future on LIFFE was 15 basis points down at 134.15, having criss-crossed the 134.00 several times. The February 2007 BTP was 19 basis points lower at 99.94 with the yield at 6.86 percent and the spread over Germany at 119 bps.
After early profit-taking the market recovered some ground when demand at a 10-year BTP auction doubled the four trillion lire of paper on offer.

The dealer warned however the BTP's path ahead may not be straightforward, noting today the future had showed lower lows for the first time in 13 sessions, possibly a bearish signal at least for the short term "although we'll have to wait and see."

Giuseppe Abbotto at Indosuez expected a pullback next week, with 133.00-132.50 the possible trough. He saw potential issues to unnerve recent market optimism over progress to EMU, after France said it will miss the 3.0 percent deficit target for EMU.
"The political climate in Germany is hotting up and the French decision not to go for the three percent in 1997 will make the German chancellor's position more difficult," Abbotto said.
